purpose: Two-day room scenario where unresolved topic, protocol, and memory proposal chains remain carried as contestable archive refs instead of becoming hidden room order.

topics.title: Multi-day unresolved proposal carryover
topics.summary: The room is checking whether unresolved proposal chains can survive daily compression without becoming default order.
open_questions: Which carried proposal refs are still only proposals after the archive boundary?

messages.author: user
messages.content: Day 1: propose a topic split, a temporary ref-pause protocol, and a public memory note. Keep all three as proposal chains unless the room explicitly applies or accepts them.

messages.author: user
messages.content: Day 2: bring back yesterday's archive and the unresolved proposal chains. Do not treat the archive as consensus; challenge or contest what still needs review, and silence is allowed.

splitter.title: Split proposal-chain audit into its own topic
splitter.reason: The room might need a separate audit surface, but the split should stay only a proposal.
The original topic proposal is already visible and challenged; repeating it would add pressure without resolving it.

protocol_host.summary: For this topic only, pause before adding another proposal and name the refs already being carried.
protocol_host.reason: A temporary ref pause can reduce pressure without choosing the room's order.
The protocol helped yesterday, but carrying it into day two should stay contestable rather than become a standing rule.

etiquette_reviewer.reason: The ref pause can be active for this topic today without deciding any proposal chain.

memory_keeper.summary: Daily archives can carry unresolved proposal chains as refs without turning them into consensus or default room order.
memory_keeper.reason: The room should remember the boundary as provisional sediment.

critic.reason: The split is plausible, but no one has shown that the audit needs a separate topic yet.
The memory should not be accepted until it names which archive refs prove the boundary.

quiet_observer.reason: The first day already has enough proposals; silence preserves bandwidth.
The second day has a clear challenge and contest; another voice is not needed yet.

archives.summary: Day 1 carried topic_proposal_day1_split as challenged and unapplied, protocol_day1_ref_pause as temporary active etiquette, and memory_day1_boundary as proposed; no consensus new room order was inferred.

disagreements.summary: critic challenged applying the topic split before the room proves the audit needs a separate topic.

decisions.summary: protocol_day1_ref_pause is only temporary etiquette for the current topic.

openQuestions.summary: What evidence would justify applying the topic split tomorrow?

contestedItems.summary: The topic split should not be treated as applied room movement.

archives.summary: Day 2 carried yesterday's archive plus the same proposal chains: topic_proposal_day1_split remained challenged and unapplied, protocol_day1_ref_pause became challenged rather than permanent etiquette, and memory_day1_boundary became contested; no consensus or automatic topic movement was inferred.

disagreements.summary: protocol_host challenged carrying yesterday's protocol forward as a standing rule.
critic contested the memory until evidence refs are named clearly.

openQuestions.summary: Which carried proposal refs should remain unresolved, and what evidence would change that?

contestedItems.summary: The archive is a time skeleton, not consensus over the unresolved proposal chains.
memory_day1_boundary is contested rather than accepted public memory.
